about.title: Buena Park Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Buena Park sits where Beach Boulevard crosses SR-91, and a good share of Orange County traffic funnels through on any given day. In 2025, the city's public collision records closed out with 338 injury crashes, 483 people hurt, and 8 lives lost. Those reports cluster along Beach Boulevard, SR-91, La Palma Avenue, and Western Avenue, and they tend to stack up on Friday evenings between 5 and 7. If one of those numbers is you, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the bruises. LawProactive exists to take one task off your plate. Tell us what happened, and we connect you, at no cost, with an independent car accident attorney who handles Orange County claims. That lawyer works on contingency, so nothing comes out of your pocket unless money is recovered. Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible; your share is simply reduced by your percentage. Most claims carry a two-year deadline, sometimes only six months when a public agency is involved, so starting early matters.

whyChoose.title: Why Buena Park Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Nothing Owed Unless You Recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network takes car accident cases on contingency. Our connection is free, and the lawyer's fee comes only out of a recovery, never your savings.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Close the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so being 20 or even 60 percent responsible reduces your claim rather than erasing it. And there is no state cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life.

items.title: Deadlines and Evidence Handled Early
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, but only six months to give notice if a city or state vehicle was involved. Getting an attorney involved quickly helps lock down dashcam footage, witness contacts, and repair records before they disappear.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Beach Boulevard near the 91 and the other driver's insurer keeps calling. Do I have to give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: No. You are not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use an offhand comment about the merge or your speed to argue you share blame. Let the lawyer handle those conversations while you focus on treatment.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Buena Park?
items.answer: California gives most injury victims two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit. If a government vehicle or a road maintained by a public agency played a role, you may have only six months to submit a formal claim. Because of that shorter window, it helps to have an attorney review the facts right away.

items.question: What should I save after a crash in Buena Park?
items.answer: Keep photos of every vehicle and the intersection, the police report number, medical bills, and the names of anyone who stopped to help. If the collision happened near a business on La Palma or Western, ask whether their cameras caught it, since footage is often overwritten within days. Your attorney can send preservation requests, but noting these details early makes that job much easier.
